short_title: perpendicular at extremity of a diameter is tangent
enunciation: The straight line drawn at right angles to the diameter of a circle from its extremity will fall outside the circle, and into the space between the straight line and the circumference another straight line cannot be interposed; further the angle of the semicircle is greater, and the remaining angle less, than any acute rectilineal angle.

subslides.symbolic: / D A / = / D C / → < D A C ) = < A C D ) = ∟ ⇒⇐ → / A E / outside

/ D A / = / D C / → < D A C ) = < A C D ) = right ⇒⇐
Thus the perpendicular falls outside as / A E /.
subslides.just_title: Two angles of < A C D > would equal two right angles, contradicting I.17; so / A E / falls outside.

subslides.chapter: the horn-like angle (κερατοειδὴς γωνία) & degree of curvature
subslides.symbolic: ∠( ( C H A ), / A E / ) < θ < ∠( / B A /, ( C H A ) ) ∀ acute θ
subslides.clause_html:
The Horn-Like Angle (κερατοειδὴς γωνία)
angulus contactus → gradus curvitatis
From Democritus and Proclus to Campanus, Peletier, Clavius, Vieta, and John Wallis (1656), the non-Archimedean "angle of contact" catalyzed the transition from static angle comparison to differential curvature.
subslides.just_title: Wallis showed that at the point of contact the tangent is not inclined to the circle; their separation measures degree of curvature.
